title: Medical Groups Issue New Vaccine Guidance Amid Federal Confusion
subtitle: Doctors step in to provide clear advice on flu and COVID-19 shots for the upcoming fall season.

summary.en: Major U.S. medical organizations have released new vaccination guidelines for the fall season. This move aims to help the public navigate confusion caused by changing advice from federal health officials. Experts emphasize that vaccines remain essential for preventing severe illness, especially among high-risk groups. The recommendations cover flu, COVID-19, and RSV, providing clear information on who should get which shot. Medical groups are now using shared online platforms to ensure consistent, science-based information reaches patients.
summary.zh: 美國各大醫療組織已發布秋季疫苗接種新指引，旨在協助民眾釐清聯邦衛生官員因建議變更而造成的混亂。專家強調，疫苗對於預防重症依然至關重要，特別是針對高風險族群。這些建議涵蓋流感、新冠肺炎與呼吸道融合病毒，並針對接種對象提供明確資訊。醫療團體目前正透過共享的網路平台，確保病患能獲得一致且基於科學的資訊。

paragraphs.en: As the fall season approaches, leading medical groups in the United States have joined together to issue new guidelines for flu and COVID-19 vaccinations. This effort comes as doctors hope to clear up confusion caused by changing advice from the current administration. While federal health agencies usually provide this guidance, recent shifts in recommendations—often without new scientific evidence—have left many people unsure about what they should do to stay healthy.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著秋季臨近，美國各大醫療團體聯合發布了針對流感與新冠肺炎疫苗接種的新指引。此舉源於醫師們希望釐清現任政府因建議反覆變更而造成的混亂。儘管聯邦衛生機構通常會提供相關指導，但近期建議的頻繁變動（且往往缺乏新的科學證據支持），已導致許多民眾對於如何維持健康感到無所適從。

paragraphs.en: According to The Guardian Health and MedPage Today, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has not provided clear updates on fall guidance. Furthermore, the advisory panel that usually helps shape these policies is currently involved in a difficult court battle. Because of this, major organizations, including the American Academy of Pediatrics and the American Medical Association (AMA), have stepped in to fill the gap. These groups are now sharing consistent, science-based information on a dedicated website to ensure the public has reliable facts while the federal process remains uncertain.
paragraphs.zh: 根據《衛報健康版》（The Guardian Health）與《MedPage Today》報導，美國疾病管制與預防中心（CDC）尚未針對秋季指引提供明確的更新。此外，通常協助制定這些政策的諮詢小組目前正陷入一場棘手的法律訴訟。因此，包括美國兒科學會（American Academy of Pediatrics）與美國醫學會（American Medical Association, AMA）在內的主要組織已介入填補空缺。這些團體目前正透過專屬網站分享一致且基於科學的資訊，以確保在聯邦程序仍不明朗的情況下，大眾能獲得可靠的事實依據。

paragraphs.en: For the flu vaccine, medical societies agree that almost everyone starting at the age of six months should get a shot. The flu can be particularly dangerous for young children, pregnant women, and people over the age of 65. It is also a serious risk for those with long-term health conditions like asthma, diabetes, or heart disease. The last two flu seasons were especially difficult, with a high number of child deaths, most of which occurred in children who had not been vaccinated. While vaccines cannot stop every infection, they are very good at preventing the worst outcomes. According to the Vaccine Integrity Project at the University of Minnesota, these shots help decrease hospital stays for older adults by 31 percent.
paragraphs.zh: 針對流感疫苗，醫學界一致認為，除了六個月以上的嬰幼兒外，幾乎所有人都應接種。流感對幼童、孕婦及六十五歲以上長者而言特別危險。對於患有氣喘、糖尿病或心臟病等長期健康問題的人來說，流感亦構成嚴重威脅。過去兩個流感季的情況尤為嚴峻，兒童死亡人數偏高，且大多數死亡案例皆未接種疫苗。雖然疫苗無法阻絕所有感染，但對於預防最嚴重的後果極為有效。根據明尼蘇達大學（University of Minnesota）的疫苗誠信計畫（Vaccine Integrity Project）指出，這些疫苗能協助長者減少百分之三十一的住院率。

paragraphs.en: There are several options available this year. For seniors, there are three "enhanced" vaccines designed to provide better protection. Doctors suggest that if one of these is not available, people should not wait, but instead get whatever vaccine they can find. Additionally, there is a new choice for people aged 50 and older. This is the first flu vaccine made with mRNA technology, the same type of technology that was very important during the COVID-19 pandemic. A study found that this new option, called mFlusiva, was 27 percent more effective at preventing symptoms in people aged 50 to 64 compared to a standard shot. For those who do not like needles, a nasal spray called FluMist is also an option for people between the ages of 2 and 49, provided they meet certain health requirements.
paragraphs.zh: 今年有幾種疫苗可供選擇。針對長者，市面上有三款旨在提供更佳保護力的「加強型」疫苗。醫師建議，若無法取得其中任何一款，民眾不應等待，應儘速接種手邊能取得的疫苗。此外，五十歲及以上的民眾還有新的選擇，這是首款採用信使核糖核酸（mRNA）技術製成的流感疫苗，該技術在新冠肺炎大流行期間發揮了關鍵作用。一項研究發現，這款名為 mFlusiva 的新選擇，在預防五十至六十四歲族群出現症狀的效力上，比標準疫苗高出百分之二十七。對於畏懼針頭的民眾，若符合特定健康條件，二至四十九歲的人群亦可選擇名為 FluMist 的鼻噴劑型疫苗。

paragraphs.en: Regarding COVID-19, the situation is different than it was in previous years. While federal agencies once recommended the vaccine for almost everyone, the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has now formally approved the shots primarily for higher-risk groups. This includes people aged 65 and older and younger individuals who have specific health concerns. The medical groups are also reminding the public about the risk of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), another common illness that becomes a concern during the colder months.
paragraphs.zh: 關於新冠肺炎，情況與往年有所不同。過去聯邦機構曾建議幾乎所有人接種疫苗，但美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）目前已正式核准將疫苗主要用於高風險族群，包括六十五歲及以上長者，以及患有特定健康問題的年輕族群。醫療團體也提醒大眾注意呼吸道融合病毒（RSV）的風險，這是另一種在寒冷月份容易引發擔憂的常見疾病。

paragraphs.en: Dr. Sandra Fryhofer of the American Medical Association noted that there has been a lot of chaos regarding these recommendations. By working together, these medical societies hope to provide a clear path forward for patients. They are focusing on the science behind the shots to help people make informed decisions for themselves and their families. As the fall season begins, the message from these doctors is simple: stay informed, talk to your healthcare provider, and do not delay in protecting yourself against preventable respiratory illnesses.
paragraphs.zh: 美國醫學會的桑德拉·弗萊霍弗（Sandra Fryhofer）醫師指出，這些建議目前存在許多混亂。透過共同合作，這些醫學會希望為病患提供明確的指引。他們正專注於疫苗背後的科學根據，以協助民眾為自己及家人做出明智的決定。隨著秋季到來，醫師們傳達的訊息很簡單：保持資訊靈通、與您的醫療照護提供者諮詢，並儘速採取行動，預防可避免的呼吸道疾病。

keyTerms.definitionEn: To resolve or remove confusion or uncertainty.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作「收拾房間」，這裡指解決混亂。文中：This effort comes as doctors hope to clear up confusion caused by changing advice from the current administration.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To become involved in a difficult situation to provide help.
keyTerms.noteZh: 這裡指在他人缺席時主動介入補位。文中：Because of this, major organizations, including the American Academy of Pediatrics and the American Medical Association (AMA), have stepped in to fill the gap.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To influence the development or nature of something.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（形狀），這裡作動詞用。文中：Furthermore, the advisory panel that usually helps shape these policies is currently involved in a difficult court battle.

quiz.question: What does the article state about the effectiveness of the new mFlusiva vaccine?

options.A: It is 31 percent more effective at preventing hospital stays for seniors.
options.B: It is 27 percent more effective at preventing symptoms in people aged 50 to 64 than a standard shot.
options.C: It is the only vaccine recommended for people aged 50 and older.
options.D: It is a nasal spray option designed for those who dislike needles.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第四段，研究顯示 mFlusiva 對於 50 到 64 歲的人群，在預防症狀方面比標準疫苗有效 27%。選項 A 提到的 31% 是指一般疫苗對老年人減少住院率的數據，而非 mFlusiva 的效能。選項 C 錯誤，因為文章僅提到這是一個新選擇，並非唯一選擇。選項 D 錯誤，因為 FluMist 才是鼻噴劑，mFlusiva 是 mRNA 技術疫苗。

quiz.question: Based on the text, why have major medical organizations decided to create their own website for vaccine information?

options.A: They want to compete with the CDC for public funding.
options.B: They believe the federal government is no longer capable of conducting scientific research.
options.C: They are concerned that the lack of clear, consistent federal guidance is causing public confusion.
options.D: They want to promote specific brands of vaccines over others.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據第一段與第二段，聯邦機構（如 CDC）近期提供的建議缺乏科學證據且變動頻繁，導致民眾感到困惑。因此，醫療組織介入是為了填補這個資訊空缺，提供穩定且基於科學的建議。選項 A 與 D 在文中皆無提及。選項 B 錯誤，文中提到的是聯邦程序不確定性及法律糾紛，而非質疑其研究能力。

quiz.question: In the first paragraph, what does the phrase 'clear up' mean in the context of the doctors' efforts?

options.B: To physically clean a specific area.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。在文中，「clear up confusion」意指「消除或解決混亂」。這是在描述醫生們希望透過提供一致的資訊，來化解大眾對於疫苗建議變來變去的困惑。選項 B 是字面上的「清理」，不符合語境。選項 C 與 D 皆與文中討論的資訊傳遞與釐清事實的語意不符。

quiz.question: What is the primary message of the article?

options.A: The federal government has completely stopped providing vaccine recommendations.
options.B: mRNA technology is the only safe way to prevent the flu.
options.C: Medical groups are providing reliable, science-based guidance to help the public navigate vaccination decisions this fall.
options.D: The flu is now considered more dangerous than COVID-19 for all age groups.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。全文的核心主旨在於說明，由於聯邦政府的建議缺乏一致性，專業醫療團體聯合起來，透過科學證據提供清晰的疫苗指引，以協助大眾在秋季做出正確的健康決策。選項 A 過於誇大，政府並未停止建議。選項 B 文中未提及這是「唯一」安全方式。選項 D 錯誤，文中僅提到流感對特定高風險族群危險，並未比較流感與新冠的危險程度。
